thread.title: Get correlation between columns in pandas without using .corr()?

author: Coolio2654
title: Get correlation between columns in pandas without using .corr()?
text:
up vote 0 down vote favorite
So, I am familiar with some more advanced Pandas indexing and with using .apply() on columns/rows of data, but for some reason I cannot figure out how to get a variance-covariance matrix for some Pandas columns.
Whenever I try the following to slice the columns I want (all rows, and all columns after "APPL R"), a = np.cov(data1.loc[:,'AAPL R':])
I get an answer like array([[ 7.27823733e-04, 2.26078140e-04, 1.99410574e-04, ..., 9.57801851e-05, -2.76751908e-04, 5.71509542e-05], [ 2.26078140e-04, 1.26173616e-04, 2.17306383e-04, ..., 3.30070375e-05, -2.47989495e-05, 1.16819595e-05], [ 1.99410574e-04, 2.17306383e-04, 1.92984210e-03, ..., -2.27400788e-04, -4.46589343e-05, -5.90865613e-05], ..., [ 9.57801851e-05, 3.30070375e-05, -2.27400788e-04, ...,
How could I manually get a simple output like this from Pandas?
Thank you in advance.
